soru: Would you trust an old bridge?
aciklama:
Every bridge is in a quiet war against physics - wind, resonance, and metal fatigue. Here is how bridges actually fail, and why the ones you cross survived.

#shorts #engineering #science #howitworks #disaster

sahneler.metin: Every bridge is fighting a quiet war against physics.
The biggest enemy is not weight. It is the wind.
Wind makes a bridge sway, and if that rhythm matches the bridge, it grows.
Engineers call this resonance, and it can tear steel apart.
Metal also gets tired. Every single flex leaves a tiny crack.
Over the years those cracks spread until the metal simply gives way.
Add rust, overloading, or one weak bolt, and the whole thing can fail.
That is why modern bridges are tested in wind tunnels and inspected constantly.
The bridges you cross every day learned from the ones that fell.
